instruction: Count how many customers have an 'Old ID' value greater than 1000 and write the count in cell E2.

metadata.explanation: Task requires counting how many Old ID values in column C (rows 2-30) are greater than 1000 and writing the count to cell E2. Verified with Python: analyzing all 29 Old ID values, 9 values are greater than 1000 (specifically: 3604, 6540, 6603, 13500, 21540, 1716, 5606, 3209, 2420). The evaluator checks if cell E2 contains the value 9. Custom getter reads the Excel file and extracts the value from cell E2, custom metric compares it against the expected count.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: Full score (1.0) if cell E2 contains 9 (within tolerance of 0.01), otherwise 0.0

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly checks cell E2, which is the exact cell mentioned in the instruction
Getter logic correctly extracts the cell value using openpyxl from the saved Excel file
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule', using expected.get('value') directly
Metric correctly compares numeric values with tolerance support (0.01)
Expected value of 9 is semantically correct - matches the actual count of Old ID values > 1000
Postconfig appropriately saves the file (Ctrl+S) to ensure changes are persisted before verification
Complete coverage: instruction has one requirement (write count to E2) and evaluator checks E2
Data flow is correct: user performs count -> writes to E2 -> file saved -> getter reads E2 -> metric compares
